summary:

detailed_description:
The target remains live-action natural-history footage with the same cloudy coastal daylight, documentary optics, and realistic color response as the protected source.
[Shot 1] Treat the supplied source target as the authoritative edit plate. Preserve its original camera trajectory, lens behavior, framing, cloudy lighting, sand, shallow water, distant shoreline, depth of field, source motion timing, and every protected pixel. Inside the editable lower-central beach region only, rebuild the visible moving crabs as coherent instances of <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>. The source frames supply each selected crab's position, grounded lateral movement, action phase, speed, perspective, scale, occlusion timing, and motion blur; <Picture 1> supplies the visible species anatomy, shell color, leg color, claw shape, eyes, and wet surface detail. Keep feet in contact with the sand and water, reproduce plausible contact shadows and tiny reflections, and maintain stable anatomy from frame to frame. Blend the generated animals cleanly into the protected plate without a halo, border flicker, duplicated limbs, or changes to nearby unmasked crabs. Do not introduce sculptures, stylization, text, a new camera move, a new background, or a cut.

overall_soundscape:
Reuse the protected synchronized source soundtrack exactly as the complete final soundtrack. Generate no replacement sound.

nodes.title: START HERE • 0.6
widgets_values:
0.6 RELEASE • Ref2V Masked Video Inpaint

1. Install models and extra packs listed in example_workflows/README.md.
2. Copy the supplied assets to ComfyUI/input; select source media where requested.
3. Set a unique project run name, then edit scenes and the Generation Profile.
4. Follow the numbered columns left → right and inspect the saved results.

Recovery is disabled by default. Enable it only to assemble saved clips without sampling.
Workflow-specific setup and detailed wiring notes:
example_workflows/guides/Ref2V Masked Video Inpaint - MiniMax H3 0.6.md
